facts.claim: IATA says nearly half of air accidents investigated under international rules still lack published final reports, with the publication rate close to 50%.
A February 2025 joint position paper found 140 of 268 accidents recorded by IATA between 2018 and 2023 had completed investigations as of June 30, 2024; 128 cases, or 48%, lacked final reports.
IATA's March 2026 safety report cited a 63% completion rate for accidents from 2019 through 2023, covering a different period and snapshot from the February 2025 figures.

ICAO Annex 13 calls for a preliminary report within 30 days and a final report as soon as possible, ideally within 12 months, with an interim statement on each anniversary if the investigation remains open beyond a year.
The Air India Boeing 787 crashed on June 12, 2025 shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad, killing 260 people, 241 aboard and 19 on the ground, with no confirmed date for a final report.
China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735 crashed in March 2022 killing all 132 people aboard, and its investigation has no publicly available final findings more than four years later.
IATA's 2025 Annual Safety Report recorded 51 accidents across 38.7 million commercial flights, or 1.32 accidents per million sectors, down from 1.42 in 2024.

zh.title: IATA：近半空難調查未公布最終報告　飛安教訓難以傳開
zh.summary: 國際航空運輸協會指出，依國際規則調查的空難中近半數至今未公布最終報告，航空業因此難以從事故中汲取教訓；印度航空171號班機與中國東方航空5735號班機的調查至今皆無最終報告。
body: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）指出，依國際規則調查的空難中，近半數至今未公布最終報告。IATA飛安總監馬克·瑟爾（Mark Searle）表示，最終報告的公布率長期維持在約50%，在11月12日蒙特婁國際航空安全高峰會上稱此一停滯令人無法接受。IATA警告，報告付之闕如使航空業難以辨識危險因子、預防類似事件重演。

2025年2月公布的聯合立場文件統計，IATA記錄的2018年至2023年268起事故中，截至2024年6月30日僅140起完成調查，其餘128起、即48%缺乏最終報告。IATA另於2026年3月飛安報告中引用2019年至2023年事故63%的完成率，但兩組數據涵蓋期間與統計時點不同，不宜直接比較。根據國際民用航空組織（ICAO）《公約》附件13，調查國應於30天內提出初步報告，並盡快公布最終報告，理想期限為12個月；若調查超過一年仍未完成，應於每週年公布期中聲明，說明進度與已發現的飛安問題。附件13調查的目的在於預防事故，而非歸咎責任或認定法律責任。

兩起指標案件凸顯缺口：2025年6月12日印度航空波音787客機自阿默達巴德起飛後不久墜毀，共260人罹難，包括機上241人與地面19人，調查單位已在事故一週年公布期中更新，但尚未確認最終報告何時出爐；2022年3月中國東方航空MU5735班機墜毀，機上132人全數罹難，事發逾四年仍無公開的最終調查結果。儘管如此，整體飛安紀錄依然穩健：IATA《2025年年度飛安報告》統計，3870萬架次商業航班中共發生51起事故，相當於每百萬航段1.32起，低於2024年的1.42起。

en.title: IATA: nearly half of air accident investigations still lack final reports
en.summary: IATA says nearly half of air accidents investigated under international rules still have no published final report, limiting the industry's ability to learn from them; neither the Air India Flight 171 nor the China Eastern Flight MU5735 investigation has produced one.
body: Nearly half of air accidents investigated under international rules still have no published final report, according to the International Air Transport Association (IATA). IATA safety director Mark Searle said the publication rate has remained close to 50%, describing the lack of progress as unacceptable at the International Aviation Safety Summit in Montreal on November 12. IATA warns that the shortfall limits opportunities to identify hazards and prevent similar events.

A joint position paper published in February 2025 found that only 140 of 268 accidents recorded by IATA between 2018 and 2023 had completed investigations as of June 30, 2024, leaving 128 cases, or 48%, without final reports. IATA's March 2026 safety report later cited a 63% completion rate for accidents from 2019 through 2023, but the figures cover different periods and reporting snapshots and are not directly comparable. Under Annex 13 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, states should issue a preliminary report within 30 days and publish a final report as soon as possible, ideally within 12 months; if an investigation remains open beyond a year, an interim statement should be published on each anniversary. The purpose of an Annex 13 investigation is prevention, not assigning blame or determining legal liability.

Two high-profile cases illustrate the gap. The Air India Boeing 787 crashed shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025, killing 260 people, including 241 aboard and 19 on the ground; investigators issued an interim update on the first anniversary but have not confirmed when a final report will appear. China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735 crashed in March 2022, killing all 132 people aboard, and more than four years later its investigation still has no publicly available final findings. The gaps sit alongside a strong overall safety record: IATA's 2025 Annual Safety Report recorded 51 accidents across 38.7 million commercial flights, or 1.32 accidents per million sectors, down from 1.42 in 2024.
